correctness.rationale: The repaired center-locus theorem and radius are correct. The frozen endpoint proof falsely counted twenty t=2 longest normals; there are ten. Indeed the t=2 cyclic increments are a five-cube section of sum zero: four saturated increments split two positive and two negative, with the fifth zero. Per location of the zero, the three sign patterns up to negation give squared norms 14/5, 6/5 and 2, each occurring ten times overall. At t=1 range-one two-level potentials give norm-square multiplicities 4/5:10 and 6/5:20. Family B contains maximizing normals at both endpoints; the cyclic determinant is one there, so endpoint centers are unique. Interior active differences have rank four iff their graph is connected; scanning all four-edge choices and signs with exact affine feasibility intervals proves the full classification. The five-orbit norm calculation makes B uniquely maximal. Central symmetry makes the origin optimal, and the signed longest normals force every center into their annihilator. Their cyclic determinant is (t²−t−1)²; at phi the span has rank two and its complement is the frequency-two plane. The nonzero projected D orbit has ten directions (five rotations and negatives), making the decagon. Squared norms and strict rational Cauchy–Schwarz bounds prove the other inactive families cannot cut it.
